headline: Short-term law keeps FAA programs, aviation taxes, and federal drone-threat powers running through May 10, 2024.
what_it_does: This law temporarily extends many Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) programs through May 10, 2024. It keeps airport grant funding, drone pilot programs, weather reporting, remote tower testing, and the Essential Air Service program going. It also continues the taxes on airline tickets and aviation fuel that pay into the fund behind most FAA spending. Finally, it extends the power of Homeland Security and the Justice Department to act against drones that pose a credible threat to certain high-risk sites.

who_it_affects.how: Federal taxes and fees on airline tickets continue to be collected through May 10, 2024.
Taxes on aviation fuel continue to be collected to fund the Airport and Airway Trust Fund.
They remain eligible for Airport Improvement Program grants for planning, building, and noise projects.

who_it_affects.group: Residents of small and rural communities
who_it_affects.how: The Essential Air Service program, which supports air service to these communities, continues operating.

who_it_affects.group: Drone operators and drone test sites
who_it_affects.how: FAA drone test site and drone detection and identification pilot programs continue.
Federal agencies keep the authority to take action against drones that threaten certain protected sites.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted March 8, 2024; extensions run through May 10, 2024.
